title.en: Nature of services: the five I's

body.en: *Services* are intangible, so they cannot be touched and are judged by experience. They are inconsistent because each customer's need differs, inseparable because production and consumption happen together, they cannot be stored (inventory less), and they involve the customer in their delivery.

title.en: Services versus goods; types of services

body.en: Goods are tangible, can be stored, are standardised and their ownership passes to the buyer; *services* are intangible, cannot be stored, vary each time and give no ownership. Services are of three types: business services such as banking, insurance, transport, warehousing and communication; social services such as health care and education provided voluntarily; and personal services such as tourism, recreation and restaurants.

problem.en: A cinema in Mysuru has 300 seats and sells 220 tickets for the 6 p.m. show at ₹150 each. What revenue is lost for that show, and which feature of services explains why it cannot be recovered?

steps.en: A seat for the 6 p.m. show cannot be stored and sold later: inventory (less).

answer.en: ₹12,000 lost; services cannot be stored (inventory less)

narration.en: Let us work through this case together. A cinema in Mysuru has 300 seats and sells 220 tickets for the 6 p.m. show at ₹150 each. What revenue is lost for that show, and which feature of services explains why it cannot be recovered?

say.en: Let us work through this case together. A cinema in Mysuru has 300 seats and sells 220 tickets for the 6 p.m. show at 150 rupees each. What revenue is lost for that show, and which feature of services explains why it cannot be recovered?
Unsold seats equals 300 minus 220 equals 80.
Lost revenue equals 80 times 150 rupees equals 12,000 rupees.
A seat for the 6 p.m. show cannot be stored and sold later: inventory less.
So the answer is 12,000 rupees lost; services cannot be stored inventory less.
